tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.

Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

import Ern.Corpus.Runner

/-!
# Corpus MM3-H: access discipline, sections A–F, H, I (test module)

The cases of corpus MM3-H of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`, §1; non-normative
design material), run on the reference kernel and arena of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` (§60–§78), plus new cases fixed by spec clauses and the
usage scenario W3 (material §5b). This is a test module: no model module imports it.

Each case is a run from `LState.init statics` (§47) by the runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`):
`RunsTo k statics os L` states that every step is `ok` and that `L` is library-reachable and its
kernel state `Reachable` (§57). The verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of
its operation (`DeriveStep`, `TransferStep`, `IssueD`, `ResetD`, …) on the reached state and
decided by `decide`. Each docstring gives the expected verdict from the case's source (the
material, or the spec clause for new cases), the obtained verdict, the class (material §0, rule 5:
`N3` kernel, `Lib` library instance, `spec 3` another specification) and the positive twin (rule 2:
the same sequence without the faulty element, accepted). A case whose obtained verdict differs from
the expected one is kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH** with its cause; no case
is corrected.

Local shapes are lists of (parent, kind) (§72, §71.1); `lf` is a root leaf, `pt p` a part of `p`.
Place and authority identities are list indices (§38): `enterFrame` appends the locals and one
root authority per root local; `alloc` appends the shape and one root authority; `derive` and
`split` append the derived authorities; `issue` appends one block authority; `reset` appends one
(released) authority.

Not encoded here:
* section G (H30–H34b, H44, handle pools) and the usage scenarios W1, W2 (they use a handle pool):
  later wave (`HandlePool`);
* the cross-registry cases of §56 (a pool and an arena, or two pools, on one `internal`): later
  wave; only the arena registry exists here (`S56`);
* section J, out of the kernel, classified by the material: H38 get-or-insert cache (spec 3,
  flow-sensitive liveness, §25, §32); H39 suspended coroutine holding a `Modify` parameter
  (specs 2 and 3, §29, §81); H40 raw pointer used during a call (spec 3 and the boundary of §19,
  §81); H41 concurrent `writeShared` (spec 2, §18, §24, §68); H42 `defer free(x)` then
  `transfer(x)` (spec 3, `defer` is outside the kernel, §73, §81); H43 resource with a release
  obligation (resource specification, §7).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.MM3H

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus

/-! ## Test contracts and shapes (§48, §72) -/

/-- The empty test contract (§48): nothing shared, pinned, externally done or deallocable. -/
abbrev K0 : K := KD.toK {}

/-- A root leaf of a local shape (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev lf : Option Nat × Nat := (none, 0)

/-- A leaf part of the shape element `p` (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev pt (p : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat := (some p, 0)

/-- A structure 0 with the parts 1 and 2 (§40, §72). -/
def S2 : LocalShape := [lf, pt 0, pt 0]

/-- A write of `ls` rejected for every authority of the state is rejected for every authority
(§67.1: the writing authority is exercisable, hence exists, §43). -/
theorem write_rejected {s : S3} {ls : List Nat}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ Write3Pre s a ls) (a : Nat) :
    Write3Step a ls s .reject :=
  .reject fun hp => h a (List.mem_range.2 (exercisable_lt hp.exercisable)) hp

/-- A read of `ls` rejected for every authority of the state is rejected for every authority
(§66.2: the reading authority is exercisable, hence exists, §43). -/
theorem read_rejected {s : S3} {ls : List Nat}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ Read3Pre s a ls) (a : Nat) :
    Read3Step a ls s .reject :=
  .reject fun hp => h a (List.mem_range.2 (exercisable_lt hp.exercisable)) hp

/-- The preconditions of `transfer` other than local self-blocking prevention (§63.1–§63.7), the
fields of `TransferPre` but `noSelfLock`: used to show that §63.8 alone rejects a transfer. -/
def TransferPreBut638 (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
    SameShape s.P src dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src, s.Active x) ∧ AnchorOrder (transferEff s src dst) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, AnchorMoves s src x →
      ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
        OptP ((transferEff s src dst).A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
          EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) True)

/-- Decidability of `TransferPreBut638` (§63). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPreBut638 k s src dst) := by
  unfold TransferPreBut638; infer_instance

/-- The static preconditions of `issue` other than local self-blocking prevention (§77.1, §77.2),
the fields of `IssueStatic` but `dstNotIn`: used to show that this clause alone rejects. -/
def IssueStaticBut (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧ (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧
    s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True) ∧
    HasRight s .modify dst

/-- Decidability of `IssueStaticBut` (§77). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (IssueStaticBut s E region dst) := by
  unfold IssueStaticBut; infer_instance

/-! ## H. Abusive rejections (the model must accept) -/

theorem H36 : Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf], .write 0 [0], .endUse 0, .write 0 [0], .read 0 [0]] :=

9, link 10) in the storage 4, issued to 2 and 3; `A.link` holds a view (7) on `B.data`, `B.link`
holds a view (8) on `A.data`; teardown (`release` of both views, `endUse` of both node values),

    .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4, pt 5, pt 5, pt 4, pt 8, pt 8], .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4,

of a local structure (3), read, then released. Expected (material): `ok`. Obtained: `ok` (§65,

theorem H46 : Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, pt 0, lf, pt 3], .write 0 [1, 2],
    .derive 0 [1, 2] .observe, .store 2 4, .read 2 [1], .release 2] :=

Expected (material): `ok`. Obtained: `ok` (§63 last paragraph). -/
theorem H47 : Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, pt 0, lf, pt 3, pt 3], .write 0 [1],

/-! ## I. Progress -/

/-- Common arena of section I (§71, §76, §77): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator 1, values 2
and 3; storage 4 (nodes 5, 6) owned by 0, `internal` 4; block 5 on `[5]` to 2 and block 6 on
`[6]` to 3. -/
def fao : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4, pt 4],
  .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4, .issue 0 [5] 2, .issue 0 [6] 3]
/-- Run of H48 (§60, §65): 7, `Modify` on `B` (6) from its block, stored into `A` (5); 8,
`Modify` on `A` from its block. -/
def h48o : List Op := fao ++ [.derive 6 [6] .modify, .store 7 5, .derive 5 [5] .modify]
/-- State reached by `h48o` (§57). -/
def h48 : LState := final K0 [] h48o

/-- **H48** (material §1 I, class N3). A cycle of two authorities on whole nodes by direct
`store`. Expected (material): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: in the resulting state the target 6
would no longer be under exercisable `Modify` (§65.5). Twin without the first `store`: `ok`. -/
theorem H48 : RunsTo K0 [] h48o h48 ∧ StoreStep 8 6 h48.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (fao ++ [.derive 6 [6] .modify, .derive 5 [5] .modify, .store 8 6]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H49 (§60, §65, §62): the cycle of H48 closed through the helper 9, `Modify` on 6 from
7, then the helper released. -/
def h49o : List Op := h48o ++ [.derive 7 [6] .modify, .store 8 6, .release 9]
/-- State reached by `h49o` (§57). -/
def h49 : LState := final K0 [] h49o

/-- **H49** (material §1 I, class N3). The same cycle, closed through a helper authority, then
`release` of the helper. Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: `ok`, with a residual
blocking: the authorities 7 and 8 are exercisable in no mode and `reset` is `reject` (§65 last
paragraph and §27: `NoLock` is not adopted; §88: indirect blocking compatible with safety may
remain). **MISMATCH** in form (expected "to arbitrate", obtained `ok`); cause: spec change, spec
v0 now determines the verdict (§65, §88). -/
theorem H49 : RunsTo K0 [] h49o h49 ∧ ¬ h49.kern.ExercisableAt 7 .observe ∧
    ¬ h49.kern.ExercisableAt 8 .observe ∧ ResetD 0 h49 .reject :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), by decide, by decide, rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H50, `transfer` part (§72, §60, §65): structure 0 (field 1), structure 2 (field 3),
local 4; 3, `Modify` on the field 3, stored into the field 1. -/
def h50to : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, lf, pt 2, lf], .derive 1 [3] .modify, .store 3 1]
/-- State reached by `h50to` (§57). -/
def h50t : LState := final K0 [] h50to

/-- **H50**, `transfer` part (material §1 I, class N3). An authority transferred into the place
it covers: structure 0 is transferred into structure 2 while its field 1 holds 3, which covers
the field 3 = `corr(1)`. Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: `reject` by §63.8 alone
(local self-blocking prevention; §63.1–§63.7 hold; §88). Twin, the stored authority covering the
local 4 instead: `ok`. **MISMATCH** (expected "to arbitrate", obtained `reject`); cause: spec
change (§63.8). -/
theorem H50_transfer : RunsTo K0 [] h50to h50t ∧ TransferStep K0 0 2 h50t.kern .reject ∧
    TransferPreBut638 K0 h50t.kern 0 2 ∧ ¬ NoLocalSelfLock h50t.kern 0 2 ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, lf, pt 2, lf], .derive 2 [4] .modify, .store 3 1,
      .transfer 0 2] :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide, by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- State after the first five steps of `fao`, the arena created and nothing issued (§57). -/
def h50i : LState := final K0 [] (fao.take 5)

/-- **H50**, `issue` part (material §1 I, class Lib). A block issued into a leaf of its own region
(`issue(0, [5], 5)`, the region available). Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: `reject`,
static, by local self-blocking prevention alone: the other static preconditions hold and the
destination is in the region (§77.2, §88). Twin, the same issue into the value 2: `ok`.
**MISMATCH** (expected "to arbitrate", obtained `reject`); cause: spec change (§77.2). -/
theorem H50_issue : RunsTo K0 [] (fao.take 5) h50i ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 5 h50i .reject ∧
    OptP (h50i.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStaticBut h50i.kern E [5] 5 ∧
      ¬ IssueStatic h50i.kern E [5] 5) False ∧
    Runs K0 [] (fao.take 5 ++ [.issue 0 [5] 2]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [5] 5) (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Prefix of H51 (§72, §71): frame 1 with allocator 0, `v` (1) and `u` (2), written; storage 3
(element 4) owned by `v`, its root authority 3 held by `v`. -/
def h51p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .write 2 [2],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 3]]
/-- Run of H51, direct form (§60): 4, `Observe` on `v`. -/
def h51no : List Op := h51p ++ [.derive 1 [1] .observe]
/-- State reached by `h51no` (§57). -/
def h51n : LState := final K0 [] h51no
/-- Run of H51 through a helper (§60, §65, §62): 4, `Modify` on the element, held by the frame;
5, `Observe` on `v`, stored into the element; the helper released. -/
def h51o : List Op := h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .derive 1 [1] .observe, .store 5 4,
  .release 4]
/-- State reached by `h51o` (§57). -/
def h51 : LState := final K0 [] h51o

/-- **H51** (material §1 I, class N3). An element of a storage owned by `v` holds a view on `v`.
Expected (material): to arbitrate. Obtained: the direct `store` is `reject`: the view takes away
the frame's `Modify` on `v`, hence on the storage it owns (§43 case 4, §65.2, §65.5); twin with
the view on another value `u`: `ok`. Through a helper on the element, then its `release`, the
configuration is reached (`ok`); then `v` can be neither written, nor relieved of the view, nor
ended (`reject`, §67.1, §62.2, §69.1), while the view stays exercisable in `Observe`; the exit of
the frame is `ok` (§88: residual blocking). **MISMATCH** in form (expected "to arbitrate", obtained
`reject` / `ok`); cause: spec change, spec v0 now determines the verdicts (§65.2, §88). -/
theorem H51 : RunsTo K0 [] h51no h51n ∧ StoreStep 4 4 h51n.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 2 [2] .observe, .store 4 4]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] h51o h51 ∧ (∀ a, Write3Step a [1] h51.kern .reject) ∧
    ReleaseStep 5 h51.kern .reject ∧ EndUseStep K0 1 h51.kern .reject ∧
    h51.kern.ExercisableAt 5 .observe ∧ Runs K0 [] (h51o ++ [.exit]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    write_rejected (by decide), .reject (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide,
    runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-! ## New cases fixed by spec v0 clauses -/

/-- Prefix of `S63_8` (§72): structure 0 with the part 1, itself with the leaf 2; structure 3
with the part 4, itself with the leaf 5; local 6. -/
def s638p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, pt 1, lf, pt 3, pt 4, lf]]
/-- Run of `S63_8` (§60, §65): 3, `Modify` on the leaf 5, stored into the leaf 2. -/
def s638o : List Op := s638p ++ [.derive 1 [5] .modify, .store 3 2]
/-- State reached by `s638o` (§57). -/
def s638 : LState := final K0 [] s638o

/-- **S63.8** (new case, §63.8; class N3). Transfer self-blocking through a nested part: structure
0 is transferred into structure 3 while its leaf 2 holds 3, which covers the leaf 5 =
`corr(2)`. Expected (§63.8, §88): `reject`. Obtained: `reject` by local self-blocking prevention
alone (§63.1–§63.7 hold). Twin, the stored authority covering the local 6 instead: `ok`. -/
theorem S63_8 : RunsTo K0 [] s638o s638 ∧ corr s638.kern.P 0 3 2 = some 5 ∧
    TransferStep K0 0 3 s638.kern .reject ∧ TransferPreBut638 K0 s638.kern 0 3 ∧
    ¬ NoLocalSelfLock s638.kern 0 3 ∧
    Runs K0 [] (s638p ++ [.derive 2 [6] .modify, .store 3 2, .transfer 0 3]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), by decide, .reject (by decide), by decide, by decide,
    runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- State after the first six steps of `fao`: block 5 on `[5]` issued to 2, so the leaf 5 is not
available (§46, §77). -/
def s772 : LState := final K0 [] (fao.take 6)

/-- **S77.2** (new case, §77.2; class Lib). Issue into a leaf of the region when the region is
unavailable. Expected (§77.2: the condition is static and checked before an availability `fail`):
`reject`. Obtained: `reject` (`issue(0, [5], 5)`: the other static preconditions hold, the
destination is in the region and the region is unavailable). Twin without the faulty element,
the destination 3 outside the region: `fail` (§77.4), as prescribed for an unavailable region;
with an available region (`issue(0, [6], 3)`): `ok`. -/
theorem S77_2 : RunsTo K0 [] (fao.take 6) s772 ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 5 s772 .reject ∧
    OptP (s772.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStaticBut s772.kern E [5] 5 ∧
      ¬ IssueStatic s772.kern E [5] 5 ∧ ¬ Avail E [5]) False ∧
    IssueD K0 0 [5] 3 s772 .fail ∧ Runs K0 [] fao :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [5] 5) (by decide), by decide,
    fails (o := .issue 0 [5] 3) (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of `S77_6` (§60, §65): 5, `Modify` on the value 2 from its root, stored into the storage
leaf 5; the frame's `Modify` on 2 now goes through 5, held by the leaf 5. -/
def s776o : List Op := fao.take 5 ++ [.derive 2 [2] .modify, .store 5 5]
/-- State reached by `s776o` (§57). -/
def s776 : LState := final K0 [] s776o

/-- **S77.6** (new case, §77.6; class Lib). Issue into a destination that would no longer be
exercisable in `Modify`: `issue(0, [5], 2)`. Expected (§77.6, §65.5, §88): `reject`. Obtained:
`reject`; the static checks, availability and the effective right of `internal` hold, but in the
resulting state the block on the leaf 5 makes the frame's only path to 2 (through 5, held by the
leaf 5) circular, so 2 is not under exercisable `Modify`. Twin without the `derive` and `store` of
5: `ok`. -/
theorem S77_6 : RunsTo K0 [] s776o s776 ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 2 s776 .reject ∧
    OptP (s776.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStatic s776.kern E [5] 2 ∧ Avail E [5] ∧
      IssueRight s776.kern E [5] ∧ ¬ HasRight (issueKEff s776.kern E [5] 2) .modify 2) False ∧
    Runs K0 [] (fao.take 6) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [5] 2) (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of `S56` (§60, §65): from the arena of `fao` (live, `internal` 4), 5, `Modify` on the
whole storage from `internal`, stored into the value 2. -/
def s56o : List Op := fao.take 5 ++ [.derive 4 [5, 6] .modify, .store 5 2]
/-- State reached by `s56o` (§57). -/
def s56 : LState := final K0 [] s56o

/-- **S56** (new case, §56, §76.4; class Lib). A second arena on the `internal` of a live arena.
Expected (§56, §76.4): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: every other precondition of `newArena`
holds, the identity 4 is in the arena registry of live administrations. Twin, a distinct
`internal` (5) over the same storage: `ok` (§56: distinct identities are not forbidden merely
because their footprints overlap). The cross-registry cases (a pool and an arena on one
`internal`) belong to the handle-pool wave. -/
theorem S56 : RunsTo K0 [] s56o s56 ∧ NewArenaStep [] 4 4 s56 .reject ∧
    NewArenaBase s56.kern 4 4 ∧ ¬ Guard56 [liveInternals s56.kern s56.arenas] 4 ∧
    Runs K0 [] (s56o ++ [.newArena 4 5]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (k := K0) (o := .newArena 4 4) (by decide), by decide, by decide,
    runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-! ## Usage scenario W3 (material §5b) -/

/-- Run of W3, literal reading (§71, §76, §77, §60, §65): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator
1, block values 2, 3, 4 and structure 5 (fields 6, 7, 8); storage 9 (leaves 10, 11, 12) owned by
0, `internal` 6; three blocks issued to 2, 3, 4; three views (10, 11, 12), `Observe` on the
blocks, stored into the fields. -/
def w3o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, pt 5, pt 5, pt 5], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 9, pt 9, pt 9], .write 0 [0], .newArena 9 6, .issue 0 [10] 2,
  .issue 0 [11] 3, .issue 0 [12] 4, .derive 7 [10] .observe, .derive 8 [11] .observe,
  .derive 9 [12] .observe, .store 10 6, .store 11 7, .store 12 8]
/-- State reached by `w3o` (§57). -/
def w3 : LState := final K0 [] w3o
/-- State reached by `w3o` and `endUse` of the structure (§57). -/
def w3e : LState := final K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5])
/-- Run of W3 with the blocks issued into fields of the structure (§77, §60, §65): structure 2
with the fields 3 to 8; storage 9 (leaves 10, 11, 12), `internal` 3; blocks 4, 5, 6 issued into
the fields 3, 4, 5; views 7, 8, 9 derived from them and stored into the fields 6, 7, 8. -/
def w3vo : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 9, pt 9, pt 9], .write 0 [0], .newArena 9 3, .issue 0 [10] 3,
  .issue 0 [11] 4, .issue 0 [12] 5, .derive 4 [10] .observe, .derive 5 [11] .observe,
  .derive 6 [12] .observe, .store 7 6, .store 8 7, .store 9 8]
/-- State reached by `w3vo` (§57). -/
def w3v : LState := final K0 [] w3vo

/-- **W3** (material §5b, frame arena; class Lib, not given by the material). `alloc`,
`newArena`, three `issue`, three views stored into a local structure; `reset` while the views
live; `endUse` of the structure; `reset`; reissue. Expected (material): `reset` during the views
`reject`; after `endUse` of the structure `ok`; reissue `ok`. Obtained, literal reading (blocks
issued to the locals 2, 3, 4): `reject` during the views (§78.2); after `endUse` of the structure,
`reset` is still `reject`, the three blocks being held by the values 2, 3, 4 (§78.2); after their
end, `reset` and the reissue are `ok`. With the blocks issued into fields of the structure: the
expected verdicts (§78.2, §69 effect, §77). **MISMATCH** on the literal reading (after `endUse`
of the structure: expected `ok`, obtained `reject`); cause: case defect, the material does not say
which values hold the blocks. -/
theorem W3 : RunsTo K0 [] w3o w3 ∧ ResetD 0 w3 .reject ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5]) w3e ∧ ResetD 0 w3e .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5, .endUse 2, .endUse 3, .endUse 4, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 2]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] w3vo w3v ∧ ResetD 0 w3v .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3vo ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 3]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide),

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

## 1. Corpus MM3-H — discipline d'accès
## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.

**Options**

1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.

**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?

**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

---

content.content:
## 27. Consumption, Transfer, and Invalidation

A value cannot be consumed, ended, reset, or transferred in a way that would invalidate an active authority dependent on its validity. By default, transferring the whole value is incompatible with active derived authorities covering its source; exceptions are limited to transitions that actually preserve validity obligations without creating new rights.

The `transfer` operation in Section 63 (O4) is a consuming operation: it marks the source `Moved` and the destination `Init` for the relevant leaves, subject to its preconditions on shape, initialization, rights, holders, anchors, and pinning. It does **not physically move storage owned** by the value. A transfer is prohibited if an in-place leaf being moved is pinned; pinning of owned storage alone does not, by itself, prohibit transferring the value that owns it. The local self-blocking prevention rule also requires that no authority moved into a destination part cover a leaf of its new holder (O4.8).

Dependencies must remain valid after the transition (`NoDangling` and related rules). Conditions required over all control-flow paths, as well as value-passing conventions at calls, belong to Spec 3. No general guarantee of freedom from authority-blocking cycles is added to this contract.

## 28. Global Accesses Without Ambient Authority

Access to global storage, or storage reachable through several paths, cannot bypass ordinary exclusivity or observation stability. In the access discipline, **a global is static storage attached, directly or transitively, to the base frame**. A mutable global is not prohibited in principle; however, it does not confer any ambient authority on a called function.

To exercise authority over a global, the callee must receive a parameter derived and passed by the caller under the rules of `enterFrame` (Section 72, O6), then respect the corresponding effective rights and dependencies. A function's indirect effects create no exception to these rules. The representation and syntactic forms of globals are not fixed here.

## 29. Boundary of the Concurrent Model

The access discipline distinguishes values transferable between execution contexts from values whose access may be shared between such contexts. These properties follow structurally from declared leaves, composition rules, types, authorities, and associated resources; they do not follow merely from a storage address.
----
## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights

These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.

----
## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.

**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.

# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization

A leaf's initialization state and the effective right to access it are two distinct conditions.

## 66. O9 — Safe Reading of Regions

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf being read belongs to a usable place and is `Init`.
2. `access` is an authority exercisable in `Observe` mode over the region; its **effective** mode actually permits observation of each leaf being read.
3. Required anchors are valid, and the type and storage contract permits this read.

**`ok` effect:** The logical read succeeds, without modifying `F`, `P`, `I`, `A`, `D`, or arena entries. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`Moved` and `Uninit` cannot be read. This definition does not replace concrete representation and pointer checks of the elementary memory machine.

## 67. O10 — Ordinary Write

**Preconditions**

1. Targeted leaves belong to usable places, and `access` is exercisable in `Modify` mode with **effective** `Modify` right over each leaf.
2. No incompatible ordinary authority holds an incompatible effective mode over the written leaves (I1).
3. Anchors and constraints of the relevant types, storage, and abstractions remain valid.

**`ok` effect:** The logical write sets the actually written leaves to `Init` and does not modify authorities or their anchors. An unwritten leaf does not become `Init` by this effect. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 68. O11 — Write Under Shared Mutation

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf in the region is usable and declared `K.SharedMutable`.
2. `access` is exercisable in a mode **at least** `Observe` and has a present effective mode on every leaf, either `Observe` or `Modify`; exercising an authority without an effective mode is insufficient.
3. Dependencies are valid and the particular shared-mutation discipline guaranteed by `K.SharedMutable` applies.

**`ok` effect:** Actually written leaves become `Init`; authorities and their structural exclusivity I1 do not change. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`writeShared` may update metadata under an `Observe` authority when the contract permits. Stability of observed contents is not automatically guaranteed, and this kernel **does not prove** the absence of data races: that requires the concurrency model's guarantees.

# XI. End of Use, Deallocation, and Allocation

The logical end of a value does not necessarily entail deallocation of its storage. The following operations treat initialization, ownership, and physical release separately.

## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root

**Static preconditions**

1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
2. **All leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.

**Outcomes**
----
## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded). Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.

## 79. Non-Escaping Values and Returns

The second-class nature of access authorities does not prohibit constructing a value carrying a derived authority or returning a result dependent on a caller-owned resource. What is prohibited is artificially extending the validity of a local origin.

----
## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.

import Ern.Corpus.LibRunner

/-!
# Corpus: library cases (test module)

Library cases of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`; non-normative design material)
and of the corrected handle-pool contract, run on the reference kernel of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` (§60–§75), the arena of Part XIV (§76–§78), the
handle pool of `Ern.Lib.HandlePool` (contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex", non-normative, corrected by
§36 and §56: composite borrow, `resolveMany` in `Observe` without distinctness, `Modify` right on
the pool value, live pool, `newPool` on `Uninit` storage, `freeSlot` exempting `internal` and its
ancestors) and the stack of `Ern.Lib.DataStack` (contract "DS-v1", non-normative). This is a test
module: no model or library module imports it.

* Section G of corpus MM3-H (material §1 G, handles): H30–H34b, H44.
* Cases of the corrected handle-pool contract: stale, other pool, atomic and distinct batches,
  `resolveMany` in `Observe` with a repeated handle, `freeSlot` with a derived `internal`, under the
  `Modify` right only, on a dead pool, of a free slot; `newPool` on written storage; two pools on
  one storage (`pool_two_freeSlot_cross`).
* The guard of §56 across registries: a second administration (arena, pool, stack) on the
  `internal` of a live administration of another registry, or of the same registry for pools.
* The usage scenarios W1 and W2 of material §5b (W3 is in `Ern.Corpus.MM3H`).

Each case is a run from `CState.init statics` (§47) by the combined runner
(`Ern.Corpus.LibRunner`): `CRunsTo k statics os C` states that every step is `ok`, that `C` is
library-reachable and that its kernel state is reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents.
The verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of its operation on the projected
state (`ResolveStep`, `FreeSlotStep`, `NewPoolStep`, `NewArenaStep`, `NewStackStep`, `StoreStep`,
`TransferStep`, …) and decided by `decide`. Each docstring gives the expected verdict from the
case's source, the obtained verdict, the class (material §0, rule 5: `Lib` library instance) and
the positive twin of each rejection or `fail` (rule 2: the same sequence without the faulty
element, accepted). A case whose obtained verdict differs from the expected one keeps its expected
verdict and is marked **MISMATCH** with its cause.

Local shapes are lists of (parent, kind) (§71.1, §72); `lf` is a root leaf, `pt p` a part of
place `p`. Places and authorities are list indices (§38): `enterFrame` appends the locals and one
root authority per local; `alloc` appends the shape and one root authority; `derive` and `split`
append the derived authorities; `issue` appends one block authority; `reset` appends one released
authority; `resolve` appends a companion and an entry authority; `resolveMany` a companion and one
entry authority per handle. Pools and stacks are named by their registry index; a handle is
`⟨pool identity, slot index, generation⟩`.
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.Lib

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus Ern.Corpus.LibRunner
  Ern.Lib

/-! ## Test contracts and shapes (§48, §72) -/

/-- The empty test contract (§48): nothing shared, pinned, externally done or deallocable. -/
abbrev K0 : K := KD.toK {}

/-- A root leaf of a local shape (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev lf : Option Nat × Nat := (none, 0)

/-- A leaf part of place `p` (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev pt (p : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat := (some p, 0)

/-! ## G. Handles (material §1 G; HandlePool v0.4 annex) -/

/-- Pool base of section G (§72, §71, §67; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): frame 1 with the allocator
0 and the pool value 1, written, and the handle leaves 2 and 3; storage 4 (entries 5 and 6)
allocated, owned by the pool value, its root authority 4 held by it; `newPool 4 4`: pool 0 of
identity 0, slots 5 and 6, free, generation 0. -/
def pb : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 4, pt 4], .newPool 4 4]

/-- Run of H30 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the slot 0 allocated (handle in 2), freed, then
allocated again (handle in 3, generation 1). -/
def h30o : List COp := pb ++ [.allocSlot 0 2, .freeSlot 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, .allocSlot 0 3]
/-- State reached by `h30o` (§57). -/
def h30 : CState := cfinal K0 [] h30o

/-- **H30** (material §1 G, class Lib). Resolution of a handle after the release and the reuse of
its entry. Expected (material, HandlePool contract, generation; §89): `fail`. Obtained: `fail`:
the slot is live at generation 1, the handle carries generation 0 (§89: "a stale identity or
generation leads to defined failure"). Twin, the handle of the reused entry: `resolve` is `ok`. -/
theorem H30 : CRunsTo K0 [] h30o h30 ∧
    h30.pools = [⟨0, 4, 4, [⟨5, 1, true⟩, ⟨6, 0, false⟩]⟩] ∧

import Ern.Corpus.Runner
import Ern.Lib.DataStack

/-!
# Corpus DataStack: the stack library (test module)

Cases of the library instance `DataStack` of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, run on
the reference kernel (§60–§75) through the library of `Ern.Lib.DataStack`. The spec does not define
the contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
library abstractions and are not defined here"); the contract is DS-v1, non-normative, quoted in the
module docstring of `Ern.Lib.DataStack`. This is a test module: no model or library module imports
it.

* `DOp`: a kernel operation O1–O16 of the corpus runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`), or a stack
  operation `newStack`, `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow` (DS-v1).
* `dstep k D o`: the computed outcome (§58); `dstep_sound`: it is an outcome of the relation of the
  operation (`DOpRel`: the kernel relation with the stack metadata unchanged, `NewStackStep`,
  `PushStep`, `MarkStep`, `RewindStep`, `GrowStep`), `ok`, `reject` and `fail` alike.
* `druns`: a run from `DState.init statics` (§47) whose steps are all `ok` reaches a state that is
  library-reachable (`DReach`) and whose kernel state is reachable by O1–O16 (§57,
  `DReach.reachable`).
* `newStack` consults the stack registry and no other (§56, `others = []`): the library states of
  these runs hold no administration other than stacks.

Each case states the reached state with `DRunsTo`, the verdict of the step under test with the
relation of its operation on that state (decided by `decide`; `rewind_dead_fails` adds that `fail`
is the only outcome), and its positive twin (the same sequence without the faulty element,
accepted). Its docstring gives the expected verdict from its source (DS-v1; the brief; the draft
DataStack cases of the derivability material, non-normative), the obtained verdict, the class
(`Lib`: library instance) and the twin. A case whose obtained verdict differs from the expected one
would be kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH**; there is none.

Readings of DS-v1 (recorded with `Ern.Lib.DataStack`) on which a verdict depends: DS-R5 (`grow` of
a live block that is not the last one: `fail`; the draft rejected) in DS04; DS-R7 (`push` without
room: `fail`) in DS05. Every run uses the representation readings R3 (`rewind` as `split` and
`release` of `internal`, with the right of §36) and R5 (`newStack`: the preconditions of `newArena`
other than its guard, and the guard of §56). The other verdicts are the same under the alternatives
of DS-R1, DS-R2, DS-R3, DS-R6 and R4: the covering authorities lie between the top of the mark and
the top; the administrative right of §36 holds where a mark is dead or foreign; a foreign mark is
in no list of the stack; every block grown can be released; the mark removed with an older one is
both later in the list and of a higher top.

Not encoded: the draft `case_rewind_reading` (re-encoded with the library, `Witness.reading_above`);
the draft `case_static_before_fail` other than its `push` without room (its `Init`-destination
conjuncts are changed by §77.2); the kernel `newArena` conjuncts of the draft `case_stacks` (the
stack-library state holds no arena registry; the cross-registry cases of §56 are another module).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.DataStack

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus Ern.Lib.DataStack

/-- The kernel operations O1–O16 among the operations of the corpus runner (§60–§75): every
operation but the arena operations O17–O19 of Part XIV, which are not steps of the stack library
(DS-v1). -/
def kernelOp : Op → Bool
  | .newArena .. | .issue .. | .reset .. => false
  | _ => true

/-- An operation of a stack-library run (DS-v1, non-normative): a kernel operation O1–O16
(§60–§75) of non-administrative code, or a stack operation `newStack`, `push`, `mark`, `rewind`,
`grow`, with its arguments. -/
inductive DOp where
  | kernel (o : Op) (h : kernelOp o = true := by decide)

  | push (j size dst : Nat)
  | mark (j : Nat)

  | grow (j b extra : Nat)

/-- A kernel relation (§60–§75) read on stack-library outcomes (DS-v1): the kernel outcome, with
